Subject: Renewal: GPU runway reshuffle & utilization reconciliation

Hi Ellen —

Our records show SkyForge's Dedicated renewal is coming up in ~6 weeks (deal SF-2027-RENEW-42). Before we lock in tranches, we want to align capacity to your actual usage profiles so you only pay for useful headroom. Early read on your last 90d shows higher tail-width (longer peaks) than originally modeled. That affects how we recommend pool sizing and burst vs. reserve.

Can you share:
- last 90 days token/req rates and peak concurrent sessions (CSV or export is fine)
- whether you need guaranteed burst capacity during product demos (boolean)
- your preferred headroom (e.g., 15% sustained, 40% for bursts)

I've looped Ben (revenue ops) and Karthik (runtime) so we can produce two options: a conservative top-up + SLA, and an aggressive rightsize that reduces committed GPUs but adds burst credits. I've attached a short checklist and a preliminary planning doc (will follow with a formal proposal once we have your exports).

If it helps, propose a 30-min sync tomorrow to run through numbers — available 10:30–12:30 PT.

Thanks,
Mina
Head of Renewals, Redwood Inference
mina@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Thanks Mina — appreciate the proactive reach.

Attached is our usage export for the last 90 days (per your ask). High-level notes:
- Sustained concurrency has climbed ~28% month-over-month after the Q1 feature rollout.
- Peak width (90th->99th percentile duration) is longer; we saw multiple multi-hour peaks tied to customer batch runs.
- We do need demo burst capacity for a bi-weekly sales cadence (about 2 hours, up to 120 concurrent sessions).

Two quick questions:
1) Can Redwood support a mixed pool (H100 + A100) with automated routing so less-latency-critical traffic runs on A100?
2) We'd prefer to avoid an immediate large commit — can we stage capacity additions in two tranches?

I've attached skyforge-usage-export-202704.xlsx. Happy to hop on the call tomorrow at 11:00 PT.

Best,
Ellen Park
Head of Platform, SkyForge AI
ellen@skyforge.ai

Quick internal note after skimming SkyForge's export Ellen sent:
- Their recent increase is material — roughly +35% sustained token throughput relative to the baseline in the current contract.
- Peak concurrency for demo windows is the primary driver of headroom needs.

Recommendation options for the commercial thread:
A) Phased top-up (preferred): immediate +8 H100-equivalent capacity to cover current sustained + demo windows, then a scheduled +4 H100 in Q3 contingent on usage (saves committed spend if growth stalls). Estimate incremental spend ~ $XXXk/month (detailed cost sheet linked).
B) Rightsize + burst: convert 20% of current commit to burst credits, reduce committed GPUs by 12 A100-equivalents, and codify routing policies (cheap-for-batch, fast-for-latency). Lower monthly commit, higher burst usage risk.

Operational asks for either path:
- Karthik: feasibility of mixed-pool routing and cold-cache latency for A100 fallback.
- Connor: run a quick canary plan to validate auto-routing on a 50-node test window.

I can draft the commercial addendum once we pick A vs B — Mina, if you want, I’ll model a 12-month P&L for both options for Ellen.

Ben
Senior Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Renewal: GPU runway reshuffle & utilization reconciliation

Ellen — thanks for the export and for confirming demo requirements. Based on Ben and Karthik's notes, here's a consolidated plan and next steps.

Proposal (attached: runway-reslice-proposal.pdf, utilization-report-202704.csv):
1) Immediate tranche: +8 H100-equivalent reserved capacity (addresses sustained increase and demo windows).
2) Contingent tranche: +4 H100-equivalent to be triggered if 7-day rolling sustained utilization > 80% for 14 consecutive days (we'll automate evaluation and notify you).
3) Mixed-pool routing: Karthik confirms we can route non-latency-critical batch traffic to A100 and maintain an H100 fast-path for interactive/demo traffic. We will implement a canary routing window (Connor will own execution).
4) SLA tweak: temporary SLA allowance for planned canary (we'll provide an ops playbook and rollback).

Commercials: Ben will send a detailed pricing addendum and two financial models (option A: phased top-up; option B: rightsize + burst). My recommendation is Option A given your need for predictable demo performance and to reduce risk during the upcoming enterprise sales cycle.

Next steps / owners:
- Ben: pricing addendum and 12-month P&L (EOD Thu).
- Connor: canary plan and test window (target start Fri).
- Karthik: brief on mixed-pool routing constraints and expected cold-cache delta (EOD Wed).
- Ellen: confirm you approve the phased approach and we’ll generate a DocuSign addendum.

If you approve, I'll generate the addendum and route for signature — we can also stage a 30-min technical working session Thurs to align on canary metrics.

Thanks all,
Mina
Head of Renewals, Redwood Inference
